assertions.name: the_B3_word_is_a_CORPUS_statement_not_a_reconstruction
assertions.source: (s0 s1^-1)^3 is stated in binding-knots-visual-inventory-table1-data.md:12 and s1^-1 = s1 - h in categorical-proton-properties.md Step 1, so B_3 = (s0(s1-h))^3 is the corpus's word, not this probe's reconstruction. One of the two reconstruction degrees of freedom I flagged is therefore NOT open -- it was pinned all along, in a table I had not read

assertions.name: the_corpus_INFEASIBILITY_claim_is_CORRECT
assertions.source: both properties blocks assert the bare 9-crossing element B_3 x Delta_3 violates Frobenius positivity, and the neutron block names the channel ('the sigma_0 channel violates Frobenius positivity'). Checked directly: no quark-generator assignment whatsoever makes k=0 positive in every NF channel, for either nucleon. So the gluon is forced, exactly as the blocks say -- and this is what makes the selection rule non-trivial, since |tr_M| increases with k and an UNCONSTRAINED minimum would always be the infeasible k=0

assertions.name: the_rule_needs_a_CONSTRAINT_SET_the_corpus_does_not_define
assertions.source: 'minimize |tr_M|' is monotone in the gluon count k (proton |tr_M| rises 0.815849 -> 1.23196 from k=2 to k=4), so UNCONSTRAINED it returns k=0 -- the bare element both blocks call infeasible. The rule is only meaningful over a feasible set, and the corpus states the rule without defining that set in any machine-checkable way. That gap, not the value of k, is the finding

assertions.name: the_NAIVE_positivity_reading_is_REFUTED_by_the_corpus
assertions.source: categorical-proton-properties.md asserts one Hopf link restores stability, i.e. k=1 is feasible for the proton. Under the reading 'every NF channel coefficient >= 0' -- which is the neutron block's own phrasing, since it names the sigma_0 CHANNEL -- k=1 is infeasible for the proton under all 8 assignments. The reading contradicts the corpus, so the reading is wrong, and every k this probe would otherwise 'select' is therefore NOT reportable. This is why no gluon count is claimed here. Frobenius positivity must mean the Gram/LP condition G(q)x >= 0 over operator SELECTIONS, not sign-positivity of one element's NF coefficients -- and that predicate is not pinned by any block I could find

assertions.name: the_selection_RULE_EXISTS_correcting_my_own_earlier_report
assertions.source: my previous probe reported all eight quark-generator assignments on the ground that 'the corpus does not say which'. That was wrong: ilp-solution-count-unwrap.md states 'minimizing |tr_M| selects the unique sigma_0 -> sigma_0 solution' out of N_l = 84 feasible ILP solutions, and categorical-proton-properties.md repeats it. A parameter-free tie-break EXISTS and I had not found it. What blocks its use is the undefined feasible set, not the absence of a rule -- a materially different open item

description: Applies the corpus's own ILP tie-break -- minimize |tr_M|, stated in ilp-solution-count-unwrap.md and categorical-proton-properties.md -- to the nucleon gluon count, which the neutron block states inconsistently (prose says 13 crossings, its own printed net is the 11-crossing value).
